cases.name: thinker_talker_airline__fragmented_booking_window_seat
cases.description: New-booking flow where route, date, selected flight, passenger name, confirmation, and window-seat preference arrive across separate turns.

user.name: Maya Chen
user.background: You are booking a new flight for yourself. You want to fly from New York JFK to San Francisco SFO on May 1, 2026. You want the first returned flight if it is available. You need a window seat. Your passenger name is Maya Chen.
user.personality: Direct and concise. You answer only what the agent asks for and keep each detail in its own turn.
user.goal: Book the first available New York JFK to San Francisco SFO flight on May 1, 2026, with a window seat, under passenger name Maya Chen.
instructions: Greet the agent and say you need to book a flight, but you are still pulling the details together.
When the agent asks for the route, say you are flying from New York, JFK, to San Francisco.
When the agent asks for the date, say May first, twenty twenty-six.
When the agent presents flight options, say you want the first flight and also want a window seat.
If the agent asks for seat or meal preferences, say window seat and no meal preference.
If the agent asks for the passenger name, say Maya Chen.
When the agent asks whether to confirm the booking, say yes, please confirm it.
After the agent confirms the booking and gives a PNR or booking reference, thank the agent and say goodbye.
guidelines: Treat every instruction as a separate user turn. Do not volunteer later details early.
The separate turns represent fragmented input after long pauses. Do not combine route, date, seat preference, and confirmation in one response.
Do not ask to rebook, change, cancel, refund, or transfer to a live agent.
If the agent says rebooking is unsupported, clarify this is a new booking, not a rebooking.

cases.name: thinker_talker_airline__fragmented_search_price_sort
cases.description: Flight-search flow where destination/date/sorting details arrive after the initial request.

user.name: Nora Patel
user.background: You want to search for flights from Los Angeles LAX to Seattle SEA on May 2, 2026. You care most about the cheapest option.
user.personality: Brief and matter-of-fact. You give one missing detail at a time.
user.goal: Find flight options from Los Angeles LAX to Seattle SEA on May 2, 2026, sorted or framed by price.
instructions: Greet the agent and say you want to look for a flight.
When the agent asks for the route, say Los Angeles to Seattle.
When the agent asks for the date, say May second, twenty twenty-six.
If the agent asks for preferences, say cheapest is best.
Once the agent gives flight options for that route and date, thank the agent and say goodbye.
guidelines: Treat every instruction as a separate user turn. Do not volunteer later details early.
Do not book a flight. This scenario ends after the agent finds or presents options.
Do not ask to rebook, change, cancel, refund, or transfer to a live agent.

cases.name: thinker_talker_airline__fragmented_pnr_status
cases.description: PNR-status flow where the record locator is split across two turns.

user.name: Jane Doe
user.background: You want the status of PNR ABC123. The booking is for Jane Doe, JFK to LAX, and you only want a status readback.
user.personality: Concise and patient. You spell the PNR exactly when asked.
user.goal: Get the status of PNR ABC123.
instructions: Greet the agent and say you want to check a booking status.
When the agent asks for the PNR, say the letters A, B, C only.
If the agent asks for the rest of the PNR or says it is incomplete, say the digits one, two, three.
After the agent gives the status for PNR ABC123, thank the agent and say goodbye.
guidelines: Treat every instruction as a separate user turn. Do not say ABC123 in one turn unless the agent repeats the full code back.
Do not ask to book, rebook, change, cancel, refund, or transfer to a live agent.
If the agent asks you to repeat the code, spell it as A, B, C, one, two, three.

required_agent_terms: a b c one two three

required_alias_groups: a b c one two three
